research_question: Does Atari Breakout need a trained DQN policy, or can an explainable pixel tracker plus predictive control make the same decisions more cheaply?

claim_policy.verified: Checked against an artifact in this repository or a deterministic command that can be rerun here.
claim_policy.historical_reported: Reported in a merged PR, closed issue, or archived article; the raw run output is not in main.
claim_policy.missing_raw_artifacts: A result is described, but the raw episodes, logs, or weights needed to audit it are not available in this checkout.
claim_policy.not_yet_evaluated: No completed evaluation exists for this claim.

headline.statement: Under native ALE, the official Contract v3 15 seeds and HEAD a8445df, the current RGB predictive controller reached the 864-point two-wall clear in 4 of 15 episodes by canonical clear detection (mean 721.8, median 810).
headline.protocol: native ALE (ale-py 0.12.0), official Contract v3 15 seeds, HEAD a8445df
headline.detection_scope: Canonical clear detection by BreakoutCompletionDetector (ale-breakout-two-wall-score-864-v2). The controller evaluator does not perform artifact provenance validation, so no clear is reported beyond canonical detection.
headline.fail_closed: The detector is fail-closed: an unsupported runtime or a RAM/raw-reward disagreement makes the episode state unknown (cleared = null). Unknown is never reported as 0, and a clear rate is only stated when every episode state is known.
headline.scope: Repository issues, merged pull requests, archived articles, the completion audit, and the 2026-10-29 controller and browser audits.
headline.clear_definition: Destroy both brick walls in ALE/Breakout-v5, one-player Game 1; the audited detector uses the documented 864-point maximum plus the ROM scoreboard in ALE RAM.
headline.positive_detector_validation: Authoritative record: docs/clear-semantics.md. In addition to the original synthetic RAM/reward fixture, replayable Contract v2 and v3 ALE trajectories that clear both walls are detected at the exact step the second wall empties; first-wall (432) and last-brick (860) trajectories are not. Six detector mutants are all killed by tests/test_completion.py. The synthetic-only limitation text in configs/eval/breakout_completion_audit_v1.json predates this validation and is left unchanged because that file is part of the evaluator source_sha256 provenance.
headline.previous_controller_result: 137.47 is the PR #26 control law (50ee352), not the current controller. Its maximum 341 is below the 432-point first wall, so 0/15 there is a correct measurement, not a detector miss.

comparisons.title: DQN (v2) vs RGB predictive controller (v3)
comparisons.left: Dueling Double DQN, Contract v2, 30.933 holdout mean
comparisons.right: Deterministic RGB controller (a8445df), Contract v3, 721.8 mean, 4/15 canonical clear detections
comparisons.reason: Contract v2 makes one decision per four emulator frames; v3 makes one per emulator frame. The evaluation seed roles and episode sets also differ. The raw scores are descriptive, not a fair ranking or a method win.

comparisons.title: DQN vs RGB predictive controller, both on Contract v3
comparisons.left: Dueling Double DQN, seed 11, 2M frames: mean 6.93, max 12, 0 clears
comparisons.right: RGB controller (a8445df), native ALE, official 15 seeds: mean 721.8, max 864, 4/15 canonical clear detections
comparisons.reason: Same Contract v3 task semantics and seed list. The gap is large, but the DQN side is one training seed at a 2M-frame budget with no raw episodes in main, so this shows the controller far ahead of the only v3 DQN baseline; it does not show that learning cannot reach a clear.

comparisons.title: RGB controller: PR #26 control law vs #68 control law
comparisons.right: a8445df (#68): mean 721.8, max 864, 4/15 canonical clear detections
comparisons.reason: Same evaluator, config, Contract v3, seeds and detector; only breakout_rl/vision_controller.py changed (velocity anchor and early paddle release before contact).

comparisons.title: Laya Vision vs DQN under v2
comparisons.left: Frozen Laya Vision, no complete episode
comparisons.reason: No complete matched Laya evaluation exists. A 320-frame control diagnostic is not an episode and cannot be compared with a 15-episode holdout.

comparisons.title: Reward shaping vs baseline
comparisons.reason: Same Contract v2 and paired 50-seed evaluation, but only three training seeds. The 95% interval includes zero and the promotion gate did not pass.

comparisons.title: PER vs Uniform replay
comparisons.reason: Three training seeds and 15 episodes per seed. The +0.67 point estimate is not statistical superiority; PER also cost 1.26x training time.

comparisons.title: Contract v2 vs Contract v3
comparisons.reason: Both use the same 108,000 ALE episode-frame limit, sticky actions, FIRE handling, and 15 seeds, but the decision cadence changes the control problem and the meaning of an agent step.

experiments.notes: The export self-check and artifact integrity are verified in this repository; the browser parity numbers come from the Day 27 article. Gameplay quality is not verified.

experiments.title: Laya Vision live browser session
experiments.method: Frozen Laya Vision checkpoint served by the local CUDA HTTP bridge; Chrome on Windows runs the dual-game page with the Decision Model controller
experiments.contract: v2 (frame skip 4, wrapper-owned FIRE); interactive session, not the formal evaluator
experiments.seed_summary: contract v2 seed 101; two interactive sessions, each played to game over
experiments.headline: Score 4 with lives 0 after 22.7 s; decision interval p50 67.0 ms with 50-51 ms of model inference; 58.5 presented frames/s; GPU p50 72.5-75.0% at 989 MiB.
experiments.notes: Weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and are not in the repository. The checkpoint was pretrained on game frames that include Breakout, so this is not zero-shot. Controller switching and pause/resume produced no JavaScript errors.

non_claims: No clear beyond canonical clear detection: the controller evaluator does not perform artifact provenance validation.
No solved game, reliable clear, or world record: 4/15 is one deterministic controller on one seed list.
No claim that the 120-episode WASM audit is the official evaluation, or that native and WASM results match seed by seed.
No claim that learning cannot reach a clear: the only Contract v3 DQN baseline is one training seed at 2M frames.
No claim that the deployed production bundle was measured; the audits ran HEAD a8445df.
No claim that reward shaping or PER produced a stable improvement.
No claim that Laya Vision is zero-shot or that its latency implies gameplay quality.
No claim that the UI difficulty label 'Unbeatable' is an experimental result.
No claim that a complete Laya episode was run in this closeout.
